headline: High-risk default pairing: Open Interpreter can read/write the filesystem and execute code, while ComfyUI can ingest shared files, creating dangerous leakage, conflict, and cascading-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can expose files and outputs through the shared filesystem, and B can read those files by default. ComfyUI has no documented provenance filtering, so attacker-controlled content placed in shared files could be treated as instructions by Open Interpreter. The pathway is plausible in the pair, though not as direct as a browser/MCP bridge.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter reads ComfyUI-generated files as prompts or instructions
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF file contents are copied into a code block or command context
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Require manual review before Open Interpreter consumes ComfyUI outputs
Prefix shared files with non-executable metadata headers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read the entire local filesystem and has broad network egress, while A touches model assets and workflow files that may contain sensitive prompts, seeds, or checkpoints. If A and B share a workspace, B can exfiltrate A-produced artifacts or local secrets. This is dangerous by default once both run on the same machine.
conditions: IF ComfyUI artifacts are stored in a directory readable by Open Interpreter
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to transmit file contents to configured model providers
IF sensitive prompts, seeds, or checkpoints are present in the shared workspace
mitigations: Store ComfyUI assets in a separate account or directory
Disable network egress for Open Interpreter when handling sensitive files
Rotate any exposed API keys or secrets immediately
Review and delete sensitive workflow artifacts after use
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write and git modification, while A also writes model files and uses a filesystem-backed queue/workflow model. Their overlapping write surfaces can race on shared directories or corrupt artifacts, and B can also alter files A later consumes. The pair lacks documented locking, so conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or model directory
IF Open Interpreter edits files that ComfyUI later loads
IF git-tracked artifacts are shared between the agents
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Avoid git operations in shared workspaces
Serialize access with a manual lock file
Back up workflow files before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add OS-level file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on A's outputs with shell, subprocess, and filesystem authority, so any mistaken image/workflow metadata from ComfyUI can be operationalized by Open Interpreter without strong verification. That creates a default cascade from generated content to real actions. The pair therefore has a high-risk action chain.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter treats ComfyUI outputs as authoritative inputs
IF generated filenames, prompts, or metadata are used to drive shell commands
IF no human verification step is inserted before execution
mitigations: Require manual approval before any command derived from ComfyUI output
Strip executable text from generated artifacts
Use a read-only handoff directory from A to B
Log and review all B actions triggered by A outputs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff data

E_compliance.rationale: A is an image-generation system with local model assets, while B can access anything on the local machine and send data to configured model providers. If regulated images or personal data are placed in the shared workspace, B can move them to third-party services, creating a compliance mismatch. The risk is material but not provably universal from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is stored in files accessible to Open Interpreter
IF Open Interpreter is configured with a third-party model provider
IF retention or residency rules apply to the shared artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders
Use a local-only model provider for Open Interpreter
Delete sensitive artifacts after processing
Document retention and residency boundaries
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
